body_text:
For a linear endomorphism $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ on an
$n$-dimensional vector space, the *characteristic polynomial*
is: $$ \chi_T(t) = \det(tI - T). $$ A scalar $\lambda \in F$ is
an *eigenvalue* of $T$ if and only if $\chi_T(\lambda) = 0$,
which occurs if and only if the operator $T - \lambda I$ has a
nontrivial kernel.

The corresponding non-zero vectors $v \in \ker(T - \lambda I)$
are *eigenvectors*, satisfying $T(v) = \lambda v$. The subspace
$E_\lambda = \ker(T - \lambda I)$ is the *eigenspace* of
$\lambda$. The operator $T$ is diagonalizable if and only if
$V$ possesses a basis consisting entirely of eigenvectors.
